stage1.impression: A night quay with a tilted armillary globe of tinted discs on a black drum, coloured light spilling across the paving, and a canal with lit windows to the right. The coloured shadow on the paving and the window reflections in the water are the best things in the frame. The rest reads as a CG scene: the houses are one flat dark slab with identical rectangular light panels, the paving is a uniform brown tile, the sky is a saturated blue gradient with a diagonal beam artefact, the left half dissolves into an empty fog wall, and a lamp glows above the globe with no mast. Only three of the six rims read (red, blue, green); orange, violet and yellow are faint hairlines. A jury would see an intriguing object in a generic render, not a specific work standing on an Amsterdam canal.

blocking_9: The houses across the canal read as real Amsterdam canal houses: individual gables, brick texture, varied window sizes, curtains and warm tungsten interiors at different brightnesses, with no window clipped flat white
All six rims read at a glance in six distinct colours (green, orange, violet, red, blue, yellow), with violet clearly separate from blue
The background behind and left of the globe is a real place (the far quay, houses, trees, bridge lights) rather than a fog wall meeting a blue gradient
The paving reads at 1:1 as Amsterdam brick klinkers or setts with joints, wear, variation and a slight damp sheen that picks up the coloured light
Every light source has a fixture: no lamp glow floating in the sky
The plinth's blackened steel shows edge and top sheen instead of a crushed black drum
Some sign of life on the route: a bicycle against a railing, a figure far off, a bench

defects.what: Houses read as one flat box with a stepped roofline rather than gabled canal houses. No brick, identical rectangular windows, lit panels flat and near-clipped (clip 0.79% in the region, p95 240.8), muntins drawn as thin outlines
The sky is a strong blue gradient (b_median 95 vs r 33) with a diagonal light-band artefact from the top-left corner and no city glow. It reads as a backdrop
The far quay dissolves into a featureless haze band. There are no buildings, trees or lights on the far side, so the place reads as an empty void
A street lamp glow hangs above the globe with no visible mast or lantern and reads as a moon or orb (lum_median 122)

The rim glow is too weak: the orange meridian, the yellow parallel and the violet meridian are barely visible hairlines, and the violet reads as the same blue as the blue parallel. The globe's region median is 40.8, so it is barely brighter than the frame (39.4)
The plinth is a crushed black cylinder (lum_median 6.1, crush 36.7%) with no edge highlight or steel sheen, so it reads as a CG primitive
The foreground paving is a uniform, low-contrast tile (lum_range 19.8) with a regular grid, no setts, no wear and no damp sheen. It is very orange (r 54, g 30, b 21)
The coloured shadow is strong and pastel but sits on a flat surface with hard polygonal facets. It needs the paving texture to break it up
The bollards are plain cylinders with a uniform glossy red-brown finish. Amsterdammertje bollards have a distinctive shape and are dark red-brown with a cast-iron texture
Fine noise grain over the sky and the paving, and no sign of life anywhere in the frame

changes.problem: Only three of the six rims read, so the work's main idea (six glowing coloured rims) is lost and the globe is barely brighter than the frame.

evidence.measured: globe lum_median 40.8 vs frame 39.4; orange, yellow and violet rims visible only as hairlines in a 2x crop; violet indistinguishable from blue

change.to: 0.15 (and balance per colour so orange, yellow and violet match red and blue in apparent brightness)

changes.expected: All six rims read as distinct saturated lines at thumbnail size, the globe becomes the brightest coloured object, and the rims glint at their tangents.

changes.problem: The houses across the canal read as a CG slab, which is what most marks the frame as a render and denies the Amsterdam setting.

evidence.measured: clip 0.79%, p95 240.8: windows are flat white panels; facade median 19.3 with no brick variation

change.setting: the houses across: windows lit and glow, and the brick finish
change.to: 0.45 lit, glow 0.35 with random per-window variation of 0.15 to 0.5 and warmer 2400 to 2800 K interiors, curtains or interior textures inside windows, brick with mortar and soot variation, white-painted window frames catching a little light

changes.expected: The windows read as rooms with depth and varied brightness, no window clips, and the facades show brick under the window spill.

changes.problem: The sky is a saturated blue studio gradient with a diagonal beam artefact, not an Amsterdam night sky lit by the city.

evidence.measured: lum_median 51.9, b_median 95 vs r_median 33; left-edge vertical profile flat at about 50 through the top half

change.to: 0.10, desaturated toward a blue-grey with warm sodium city glow low on the horizon; remove the diagonal band

changes.expected: The sky sits darker than the houses' lit windows and the globe, and is mostly neutral, so the rims become the frame's saturated colour.

changes.problem: The globe stands against empty sky and the fog wall of an empty far quay rather than against the canal and its houses.

evidence.measured: horizon band lum_median 25.9 with no structure; the houses occupy only the right third

change.to: swing toward the canal, e.g. from [5.5, -7.0, 1.6] looking at [-1.0, 0.5, 1.6], so the lit houses and their reflections fill the background behind the globe; keep 32 to 35 mm and verticals true

changes.expected: The globe reads silhouetted against the lit houses and water, the place is unmistakably a canal, and the left void disappears.

changes.problem: The paving is a flat, uniform, orange tile that reads as CG.

change.to: Amsterdam red-brown brick klinkers in a herringbone or stretcher bond, joints, per-brick hue and value variation, roughness 0.45 to 0.6 with damp patches near the kerb; a granite kerb at the water's edge

changes.expected: At 1:1 the paving reads as brick, the coloured shadow breaks up across the joints, and lamp highlights pick out the damp patches.

changes.problem: The blackened-steel plinth is crushed to a black primitive.

change.setting: plinth finish and a street lamp aim
change.to: blackened steel with roughness 0.35 and a brownish patina so its rounded top edge and side catch the street lamp and the rims' coloured light; raise a street lamp or add a low 2200 K fill from camera-left

changes.expected: The plinth reads as dark steel with a soft vertical sheen and a bright top edge, and the shadows keep detail.

changes.problem: A lamp glows in the sky with no fixture, and the scene has no sign of life.

evidence.measured: a floating glow at lum_median 122 with no mast visible

change.from: 2 point lights with no visible fixture; no props
change.to: model the classic Amsterdam lantern on a mast for each lamp and place it in frame or out of frame; add a bicycle locked to a railing, two distant figures on the far quay, and Amsterdammertje bollards in place of the plain cylinders

changes.expected: Every light source has a fixture, and the place reads as a used canal route on a festival night.

changes.problem: Grain is visible across the flat sky and the paving, and the grade splits into a blue top and an orange bottom.

evidence.measured: visible noise in the crops; foreground r/b ratio about 2.6 against a sky b/r of about 2.9

change.to: 512 samples (or 384 with adaptive 0.01), white balance about 3300 K, so the 2200 to 2400 K lamps stay warm and the paving shifts slightly toward neutral

changes.expected: Clean shadows and sky, and a grade that reads as a single night photograph rather than a teal-and-orange split.

out_of_scope.request: Make the violet meridian's disc tint clearly violet rather than blue so it does not read as a second blue
out_of_scope.why: The discs' colours are fixed on the card. Only the rim LED level and colour balance (c1) may change. If violet still reads as blue after c1, the colour itself needs the designer's decision.

out_of_scope.request: Thicken the discs or give them polished, visibly glowing faces so they read as premium cast acrylic
out_of_scope.why: The 25 mm discs and the clear faces are fixed on the card.
